speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. How old is the baby, and when did you first notice the yellow discoloration in the eyes and skin?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool or urine, and have you noticed any other symptoms like fever or poor feeding? REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_level. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.7 mg/dL. Normal readings for stool output, urine output, fever, and feeding behavior. Normal abdominal ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The bilirubin level is significantly elevated at 16.1 mg/dL, but the direct (conjugated) fraction is normal, which rules out biliary obstruction. Has the baby had any recent blood transfusions, infections, or family history of blood disorders like G6PD deficiency?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Prolonged Breastfeeding Jaundice)
